title: Weakly supervised deep learning maps seamount morphology patterns associated with tectonic setting
summary: A weakly supervised deep-learning analysis combining satellite-derived gravity and bathymetry produced a global seamount inventory and reported systematic morphology differences: broad edifices along fast-spreading ridges and steeper forms near intraplate hotspots. The authors interpret these differences as reflecting geodynamic controls on volcanic construction. Many detections rely on indirect gravity/bathymetry data rather than shipborne mapping, so individual feature identifications and causal interpretations require further validation.
ai_technology: Weakly supervised deep-learning detector with vision foundation model, iterative pseudo-label refinement, and elliptical Gaussian fitting
organization: University of Science and Technology of China; Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory

evidence.tested: A weakly supervised deep-learning analysis combining satellite-derived gravity and bathymetry produced a global seamount inventory and reported systematic morphology differences: broad edifices along fast-spreading ridges and steeper forms near intraplate hotspots.
evidence.unknown: The publisher abstract describes numerous previously undocumented features but does not establish shipborne confirmation for every mapped detection. The reported morphology-setting relationship is an observational pattern and should not be read as proof of a unique causal mechanism.
evidence.ai_role: Detected and morphologically characterized seamount features in global gravity and bathymetry data despite sparse labels, enabling the cross-setting comparison that revealed tectonically organized morphology patterns.
